analysis: Examined head-side excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 39531-41544). This is a test-vector data file for prompt-contract golden vectors (request bodies, provider bodies, template inputs, plan block boundaries, token IDs) for gpt-oss-20b and qwen3.5-35b-a3b. The file_changes patch shows changes such as adding `additional_context: {enable_thinking:false}`, altering prompt_token_count, chain_hash values and token_ids, and removing a 768-token block boundary. These are fixture data updates with no executable code, no auth, key, attestation, encryption, billing or routing logic changes. Excerpted content contains no secrets; the `_darkbloom_prompt_date` and fixture-scope values are synthetic. Relevant threat areas are only loosely T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache; block chain hashes determine cache keys) and TB-007 (inference engine), but the fixtures only pin expected values and do not change runtime cache scoping or isolation behavior. The fixture content includes adversarial strings (Harmony framing tokens in assistant content for qwen) and presumably tests that these are stripped or sanitized; the template_input for that case drops the framing and empties reasoning_content, which is a protective expectation rather than a regression. Remaining integration question for later passes: the corresponding source changes (Swift prompt renderer, Go coordinator prompt-contract/cache-routing code) that produce the new prompt_contract_id/chain hashes and the enable_thinking context are not in the supplied units, so I cannot verify that the code matches these vectors or that the cache key derivation (scope_id, contract id) remains tenant-isolated. No finding is raised from the supplied evidence; the patch excerpt is truncated, so other changed ranges (e.g. around lines 43739-54088) were not visible to me.
